purpose: Pople-family segmented Gaussian basis sets; the suffix syntax encodes polarization and diffuse functions on heavy atoms and hydrogen.
pairs_with: an AuxJ basis for RI calculations (usually <basis>/J or def2/J); def2/J covers the Pople families only loosely, AutoAux is the safe choice
defaults: polarization via * / ** or (d) / (d,p); + / ++ add diffuse functions (see section for the full syntax)
typical_use: general small-molecule DFT and HF work; STO-3G as a minimal basis for quick tests

purpose: The older Karlsruhe/Ahlrichs valence basis sets (SV to QZVPP and the def- variants). All-electron up to Kr; the def- keywords load def-ECP beyond Rb.
pairs_with: def2/J for RI-J (all def and def2 type sets)
typical_use: older literature comparisons and quick valence-quality calculations

purpose: The Karlsruhe def2 valence-polarized basis sets, all-electron for H-Kr and with def2-ECP for Rb-Rn; ma- variants add minimal diffuse functions, -D variants diffuse functions for properties.
pairs_with: def2/J (RI-J), def2/JK (RI-JK), def2-.../C (correlation fitting); def2/J assumes ECPs beyond Kr
defaults: def2-ECP loaded automatically for Rb-Rn when the basis is requested by keyword
typical_use: standard DFT workhorse basis sets for molecules

purpose: def2-derived basis sets adjusted for the revised Dirac-Fock ECP (dhf-ECP); identical to def2 for H-Kr, -2c variants exist for two-component methods ORCA does not implement.
pairs_with: dhf-ECP for Rb-Rn
typical_use: comparisons with DHF-ECP based studies

purpose: Jensen's polarization-consistent generally contracted basis sets (pc-n, pcJ-n for NMR/EPR coupling, pcS-n for NMR shielding), plus augmented and segmented variants.
typical_use: high-quality DFT energetics (pc-n) and NMR/EPR property studies (pcJ-n, pcS-n)

purpose: Lehtola's hydrogenic (HGBS) basis sets built from one-electron model systems; the number encodes the energy-optimization threshold 10^-m, Pn the polarization shells, A diffuse augmentation.
typical_use: systematic basis-set convergence studies

purpose: Segmented all-electron Sapporo basis sets up to quadruple-zeta quality, developed for correlated wavefunction methods; DKH3-optimized 2012 variants exist.
typical_use: correlated wavefunction calculations on main-group elements

purpose: Uncontracted RHF ground-state energy-optimized primitive basis sets of Partridge; available in four sizes.
typical_use: reference primitive sets and uncontracted studies

purpose: Dunning-type correlation-consistent basis sets (cc-pVnZ) with aug- (diffuse), (+d) (tight d), partially augmented (jun/jul/apr/may/maug), core-valence (cc-pCV, cc-pwCV) and pseudopotential (-PP) variants; the standard choice for correlated wavefunction methods and basis-set extrapolation.
pairs_with: matching /C auxiliary basis for RI-MP2/DLPNO (e.g. cc-pVTZ/C), def2/J as a universal AuxJ alternative, AutoAux when no optimized aux exists
typical_use: post-HF correlated calculations and systematic extrapolation

purpose: Orbital basis sets with added tight functions for explicit-correlation (F12) methods, larger than the regular cc-pVnZ sets; they require the matching CABS (or OptRI) complementary auxiliary basis.
pairs_with: cc-pVnZ-F12-CABS or -OptRI, and -F12-MP2Fit AuxC when RI is used
typical_use: F12-MP2, F12-CCSD and related explicitly correlated calculations

purpose: Generally contracted atomic natural orbital (ANO) basis sets built on cc-pV6Z (or pc-4) primitives; more accurate per basis function than cc-pVnZ but integral evaluation is expensive; aug- and saug- variants add full or single-sp diffuse augmentation.
requires: storing all integrals on disk for efficiency; RI-JK strongly recommended for the SCF part
typical_use: high-accuracy correlated calculations on small systems; geometry optimizations are discouraged by the manual

purpose: Specialized single-purpose basis sets: D95 (Dunning double-zeta), EPR-II/III (Barone, for EPR), IGLO-II/III (Kutzelnigg, NMR/EPR), UGBS, CP and Wachters+f (first transition row), the W1 thermochemistry sets, and the Huzinaga MINI/MINIS/MIDI/MINIX minimal sets.
typical_use: EPR and NMR property work (EPR-II/III, IGLO), W1 thermochemistry protocol

purpose: Minimal STO-3G basis set covering H-I; three Gaussians per Slater orbital. Only for quick tests and teaching.
typical_use: smoke tests and illustrative examples

purpose: Relativistically recontracted variants of the old Ahlrichs basis sets for DKH2 (DKH-...) and ZORA (ZORA-...), all-electron H-Kr.
pairs_with: SARC/J auxiliary for all-electron relativistic calculations
typical_use: scalar-relativistic DKH2 or ZORA calculations on main-group systems

purpose: DKH and ZORA recontracted def2 basis sets: original def2 exponents with one contracted function per angular momentum and contraction coefficients adapted to the scalar-relativistic Hamiltonian.
pairs_with: SARC and SARC2 basis sets for the heavier elements; SARC/J as the auxiliary
typical_use: scalar-relativistic calculations on heavy main-group systems beyond all-electron def2

purpose: Segmented all-electron relativistically contracted (SARC) basis sets for the DKH2 and ZORA Hamiltonians, covering Rb-Rn and Ac-Lr (Hf-Hg for the smaller SVP variants).
pairs_with: SARC/J is the general-purpose Coulomb-fitting auxiliary for all SARC orbital basis sets
typical_use: heavy-element and lanthanide calculations with DKH2 or ZORA

purpose: Valence quadruple-zeta SARC basis sets for lanthanides with NEVPT2-optimized (3g2h) polarization functions; each has a dedicated /JK auxiliary basis set.
pairs_with: SARC2-...-QZV(P)/JK for simultaneous Coulomb and exchange fitting
typical_use: accurate correlated wavefunction calculations on lanthanide systems

purpose: All-electron basis sets optimized for the X2C Hamiltonian, H-Rn; the -s variants add tight functions for NMR shielding, the -2c variants target two-component calculations ORCA does not implement.
pairs_with: x2c/J or AutoAux auxiliary basis options
typical_use: X2C scalar-relativistic calculations, NMR shielding with the -s variants

purpose: Sapporo basis sets optimized for the DKH3 Hamiltonian and finite nucleus, K-Rn (Sapporo-DKH3-XZP-2012).
typical_use: DKH3 scalar-relativistic calculations

purpose: Correlation-consistent basis sets recontracted for DKH2 (cc-pVnZ-DK, aug and core-valence variants) and DKH3 (cc-pVnZ-DK3 for uranium).
pairs_with: matching /C auxiliary basis as in non-relativistic RI calculations
typical_use: DKH2/DKH3 correlated calculations, e.g. DLPNO-CCSD(T) with cc-pVTZ-DK and cc-pVTZ/C

purpose: The ANO-RCC basis sets of Roos and co-workers, contracted for the DKH2 Hamiltonian and covering H-Cm; Full is the complete set, DZP/TZP/QZP are double/triple/quadruple-zeta contractions.
typical_use: DKH2 calculations including actinides

purpose: OPI catalog entries gfn1Basis/gfn2Basis request the built-in minimal basis of the GFN1/GFN2-xTB Hamiltonians. The ORCA manual documents no separate basis keyword for xTB: the native xTB implementation allows no user changes to its basis.
pairs_with: GFN-xTB / GFN2-xTB Hamiltonian keywords
typical_use: semi-empirical xTB calculations (no user basis choice)

purpose: Auxiliary basis sets for pure Coulomb fitting in RI-J, RIJDX/RIJONX and RIJCOSX: Weigend universal def2/J, def2/J-based for the minimally augmented mTZVP sets, x2c/J for the x2c all-electron sets, SARC/J for all-electron relativistic work and the min/J, dgauss-aX/j small sets.
requires: an RI Coulomb approximation (RI-J, RIJDX/RIJONX, RIJCOSX)
excludes: do not use def2/J with DKH/ZORA/X2C; use SARC/J or AutoAux instead
defaults: def2/J is automatically invoked for RIJCOSX hybrid DFT; in scalar relativistic calculations the default is SARC/J
typical_use: pure and hybrid DFT energies, gradients and frequencies

keyword: Coulomb- and exchange-fitting auxiliary basis sets (AuxJK)
purpose: Auxiliary basis sets optimized for simultaneous Coulomb and exchange fitting (RI-JK): def2/JK and its reduced def2/JKsmall, cc-pVnZ/JK and aug-cc-pVnZ/JK, and the dedicated SARC2 lanthanide /JK sets.
requires: the RI-JK approximation; if such a basis is used for RI-J alone it must be assigned to AuxJ via the %basis block
typical_use: hybrid DFT and CASSCF RI-JK calculations

manual.section: 2.7.4.2 Coulomb- and exchange-fitting auxiliary basis sets (AuxJK)

keyword: Auxiliary basis sets for correlated methods (AuxC)
purpose: Auxiliary basis sets for post-(CAS)SCF dynamical correlation (RI-MP2, double hybrids, DLPNO): def2-*/C, cc-pVnZ/C and aug- variants, core-valence cc-pwCVnZ/C, pseudopotential -PP/C variants and the F12-MP2Fit sets.
requires: an RI post-SCF correlation method (RI-MP2, RI-CC, DLPNO, double-hybrid DFT)
typical_use: RI-MP2/DLPNO-MP2/DLPNO-CCSD(T) and double-hybrid DFT energies and gradients

manual.section: 2.7.4.3 Auxiliary basis sets for correlated methods (AuxC)

keyword: Complementary auxiliary basis sets for F12 (CABS)
purpose: Complementary auxiliary basis sets (CABS) required in addition to the F12 orbital basis in explicitly correlated calculations; the OptRI variants are identical bases under another name.
requires: an F12 orbital basis (cc-pVnZ-F12) and an F12 method
typical_use: F12-MP2 and F12-CCSD calculations

manual.section: 2.7.4.4 Complementary auxiliary basis sets for F12 (CABS)

purpose: Automatically generates an auxiliary basis for the chosen orbital basis, usable for Coulomb, exchange and correlation fitting; as accurate as optimized auxiliary sets but up to twice as large. Populates all three Aux slots when given in the simple input line.
pairs_with: any orbital basis without optimized auxiliary sets
defaults: AutoAuxSize 1; AutoAuxTightB true; generation factors AutoAuxF[l]/AutoAuxB[l] (see the %basis table)
typical_use: any RI calculation without a built-in auxiliary basis, especially with large or relativistic orbital bases

manual.section: 2.7.4.5 Automatic Generation of Auxiliary Basis Sets (AutoAux)

purpose: The Karlsruhe def2 Wood-Boring ECPs; loaded automatically with def2 orbital basis keywords for Rb-Rn and assignable explicitly via the ECP option of the %basis block.
pairs_with: the matching orbital basis family (see its record); explicit control via the ECP option of the %basis block
typical_use: heavy-element geometry optimizations and energies; the manual cautions that ECPs may not be the best choice for property calculations
note: ORCA 6.1.1 rejects this spelling as a simple-input keyword (probe); the ECP must be selected through the %basis block or with a differently spelled keyword.

purpose: The older def-ECP set used by the def-SVP/def-TZVP family and the MINIX/def2-m* keywords; covers Rb-Lr.
pairs_with: the matching orbital basis family (see its record); explicit control via the ECP option of the %basis block
typical_use: heavy-element geometry optimizations and energies; the manual cautions that ECPs may not be the best choice for property calculations

purpose: Revised Dirac-Fock ECPs for Rb-Rn, optimized for the dhf-XVP basis sets (also spelled dhf-ecp).
pairs_with: the matching orbital basis family (see its record); explicit control via the ECP option of the %basis block
typical_use: heavy-element geometry optimizations and energies; the manual cautions that ECPs may not be the best choice for property calculations

purpose: The Christiansen-Ross-Ermler-Nash-Bursten small-core ECP set for Li-Og, used with the CRENBL basis; originally built for SOC interactions but SOC with ECPs is not implemented in ORCA.
pairs_with: the matching orbital basis family (see its record); explicit control via the ECP option of the %basis block
typical_use: heavy-element geometry optimizations and energies; the manual cautions that ECPs may not be the best choice for property calculations

purpose: The Los Alamos (Hay-Wadt) ECPs from 1985, extended by Roy et al.; used with the LANL08/LANL2DZ/LANL2TZ basis sets.
pairs_with: the matching orbital basis family (see its record); explicit control via the ECP option of the %basis block
typical_use: heavy-element geometry optimizations and energies; the manual cautions that ECPs may not be the best choice for property calculations

purpose: The Stuttgart-Dresden (SDD) ECP family, e.g. SD(10,MDF); assignable per element via NewECP or per fragment.
pairs_with: the matching orbital basis family (see its record); explicit control via the ECP option of the %basis block
typical_use: heavy-element geometry optimizations and energies; the manual cautions that ECPs may not be the best choice for property calculations

purpose: Multi-configuration Dirac-Hartree-Fock ECPs, used as the ECP of the cc-pVnZ-PP and -PP/C basis families (Ca, Sr, Ba, Ra, U).
pairs_with: the matching orbital basis family (see its record); explicit control via the ECP option of the %basis block
typical_use: heavy-element geometry optimizations and energies; the manual cautions that ECPs may not be the best choice for property calculations

purpose: OPI catalog entry vdzp-ecp; the ECP belonging to the molecule-optimized vDZP basis set of the r2SCAN-3c family.
pairs_with: the matching orbital basis family (see its record); explicit control via the ECP option of the %basis block
typical_use: heavy-element geometry optimizations and energies; the manual cautions that ECPs may not be the best choice for property calculations
note: ORCA 6.1.1 rejects this spelling as a simple-input keyword (probe); the ECP must be selected through the %basis block or with a differently spelled keyword.

purpose: OPI catalog entry that bundles the ECP choices used by the 3c composite methods (def2-ECP/def-ECP and the r2SCAN-3c set).
pairs_with: the matching orbital basis family (see its record); explicit control via the ECP option of the %basis block
typical_use: heavy-element geometry optimizations and energies; the manual cautions that ECPs may not be the best choice for property calculations
note: ORCA 6.1.1 rejects this spelling as a simple-input keyword (probe); the ECP must be selected through the %basis block or with a differently spelled keyword.

purpose: Removes the default ECP again, e.g. to run an all-electron calculation with a basis keyword that normally loads one for heavy elements.

Decontraction keywords: remove the contraction coefficients of the orbital and/or auxiliary basis sets. Decontract covers all sets, the DecontractBas/AuxJ/AuxJK/AuxC/CABS variants one set each; useful for DKH (which decontracts internally anyway) and for ANO or generally contracted sets that otherwise slow integral evaluation.
typical_use: DKH calculations decontract automatically; decontraction mainly pays off with generally contracted (ANO) sets

purpose: Uncontraction keywords: rebuild the basis from its primitives in the same spirit as Decontract (the manual treats both under basis decontraction). The No- forms switch the option back off.
ANOBASIS / NOANOBASIS: mark a basis as atomic-natural-orbital type so ORCA can use its special integral algorithms for generally contracted sets (relevant after custom NewGTO definitions).
OPI shell_type values; in ORCA simple input these appear as the wavefunction-type keywords RHF, RKS, ROHF, RKS/ROKS, UHF, UKS and CASSCF that pick the reference determinant flavor of the SCF.
typical_use: chosen automatically by the requested method; written explicitly to force e.g. ROHF on an open-shell system

purpose: Defines the orbital basis set by library name or, inside a NewGTO-style subblock, by explicit shells.
Defines the Coulomb-fitting (AuxJ) auxiliary basis set, e.g. AuxJ "def2/J" or AuxJ "AutoAux".
pairs_with: RI-J / RIJDX / RIJONX / RIJCOSX approximations

purpose: Defines the Coulomb-and-exchange fitting (AuxJK) auxiliary basis set for RI-JK.
pairs_with: RI-JK approximations

purpose: Defines the correlation-fitting (AuxC) auxiliary basis set for post-SCF RI methods.
pairs_with: RI-MP2, DLPNO, double hybrids, RI-CC

purpose: Defines the complementary auxiliary basis set for F12 calculations.
requires: an F12 orbital basis and F12 method

purpose: Assigns an ECP by name to all elements for which it is defined.
Activates ECPs on ghost atoms (they are skipped by default); AllowGhostECP is a synonym.
Synonym for GhostECP: turns ECPs on for ghost atoms.
Decontracts all basis sets when set to true (a plain Decontract covers every basis set at once).
Decontracts the orbital basis when set to true (a plain Decontract covers every basis set at once).
Decontracts the AuxJ basis when set to true (a plain Decontract covers every basis set at once).
Decontracts the AuxJK basis when set to true (a plain Decontract covers every basis set at once).
Decontracts the AuxC basis when set to true (a plain Decontract covers every basis set at once).
Decontracts the CABS when set to true (a plain Decontract covers every basis set at once).
Assigns a new orbital basis to one element, by built-in name and/or explicit shells; shell lines follow the basis-set file format and ORCA always uses spherical harmonics.
Adds GTO shells to the existing basis of an element (or, in the coordinate section, of a single atom).
Assigns a new AuxJ basis to an element by name and/or explicit shells.
Defines a new ECP for an element: either a built-in name or a manual parameter block (N_core, lmax and the Gaussian expansion per shell).
Removes the ECP for one element.
Assigns a basis set (and, unlike NewGTO, the matching ECP) to one numbered fragment for multi-level calculations.
Assigns an AuxJ auxiliary basis to one fragment.
Assigns an AuxJK auxiliary basis to one fragment.
Assigns an AuxC auxiliary basis to one fragment.
Assigns a CABS to one fragment.
Assigns an ECP to one fragment.
Reads the orbital basis of one fragment from an external basis file.
note: probe with a missing file name only checks the keyword itself; ORCA would fail at run time on an unreadable file.

purpose: Reads the Aux auxiliary basis of one fragment from an external basis file.
Reads the AuxJ basis of one fragment from an external basis file.
Reads the AuxC basis of one fragment from an external basis file.
Reads the CABS of one fragment from an external basis file.
Reads the ECP of one fragment from an external basis file.
Reads an orbital basis from an external file in the GAMESS-US/EMSL format.
note: the probe sandbox refuses file-reading keywords, so the parser verdict is unavailable although the manual documents the keyword; test it manually before writing it into an input.

purpose: Reads the Coulomb-fitting (AuxJ) basis from an external file.
note: the probe sandbox refuses file-reading keywords, so the parser verdict is unavailable although the manual documents the keyword.

purpose: Reads the AuxJ basis (synonym of GTOAuxJName) from an external file.
note: the probe sandbox refuses file-reading keywords, so the parser verdict is unavailable although the manual documents the keyword.

purpose: Reads the Coulomb+exchange (AuxJK) basis from an external file.
note: the probe sandbox refuses file-reading keywords, so the parser verdict is unavailable although the manual documents the keyword.

purpose: Reads the correlation (AuxC) basis from an external file.
note: the probe sandbox refuses file-reading keywords, so the parser verdict is unavailable although the manual documents the keyword.

purpose: Reads the CABS from an external file.
note: the probe sandbox refuses file-reading keywords, so the parser verdict is unavailable although the manual documents the keyword.

purpose: Trims the orbital basis by a pivoted Cholesky decomposition of the metric to remove (near-)redundant functions; metric option Overlap.
Trims the AuxJ basis in the Coulomb metric to remove redundant fitting functions before the RI equations are set up.
Trims the AuxJK basis in the Coulomb metric to remove redundant fitting functions before the RI equations are set up.
Trims the AuxC basis in the Coulomb metric to remove redundant fitting functions before the RI equations are set up.
Threshold for the pivoted Cholesky trimming; values below zero let ORCA choose automatically.
defaults: -1 (automatic; 1e-16 to 1e-10 makes sense according to the manual)

purpose: Chooses the AutoAux generation variant: 0 uses the minimal effective exponent, 1 (default) raises the maximal exponent of low-l shells, 2 of all shells, 3 uses the primitives directly.
If true, raises the maximal angular momentum of the generated fitting basis to the highest value ORCA and the orbital basis allow.
Caps the angular momentum of the generated fitting basis when set above zero.
Per-shell factor by which AutoAux raises the maximal exponent (l = 0..7: s..j).
Even-tempered expansion factor per shell used by AutoAux (l = 0..7).
If true (default), uses AutoAuxB[0] for low-l shells and AutoAuxB[l] only for high-l shells.
If true, selects the deprecated ORCA 3.1 AutoAux generation procedure for compatibility; it does not reproduce the current results.
Activates the Douglas-Kroll-Hess scalar-relativistic Hamiltonian: DKH1 the first-order, DKH2 (alias DKH) the second-order form, the ORCA default order.
requires: Order 2 in the %rel block; requires relativistically recontracted or SARC-type orbital basis sets
typical_use: all-electron DKH recontracted basis (DKH-XVP, cc-pVnZ-DK, SARC, ANO-RCC); the %rel Order keyword controls the order

purpose: Activates the zeroth-order regular approximation scalar-relativistic Hamiltonian; the cheapest relativistic option, gauge-dependent and usually combined with ZORA-recontracted or SARC basis sets.
requires: ZORA-recontracted (zora-...) or SARC basis sets, SARC/J auxiliary
typical_use: geometry optimizations and frequencies on heavy-element systems (decontraction of the basis is used for gradients)

purpose: The infinite-order regular approximation, an improvement over ZORA that still avoids the gauge problems partially; variants iora/ri and ioramm/ri exist in the OPI catalog.
requires: like ZORA, recontracted basis sets
typical_use: scalar-relativistic single-point energies

purpose: The exact two-component (spin-free one-component in ORCA's implementation) Hamiltonian: the one-electron Dirac equation is decoupled exactly. Recommended by the manual over DKH and ZORA; the only of the three with analytic gradients.
requires: x2c-XVPall basis sets (or SARC/AutoAux) and x2c/J or AutoAux auxiliary basis
typical_use: NMR shieldings (x2c-...-s basis variants), DLPNO and double-hybrid NMR with X2C

purpose: Alias of DKH2: activates the second-order Douglas-Kroll-Hess Hamiltonian (the default order of the %rel Order keyword).
Enables the diagonal local approximation (DLU) of the X2C unitary transformation; X2C only.
Enables the one-center approximation: the relativistic model potential keeps only one-center terms, which removes picture-change effects for gradients and makes optimizations cheap.
defaults: enabled by default for DKH and ZORA analytic gradients

purpose: Disables both the one-center and the DLU approximations (full two-component-free relativistic treatment).
Adds the first-order perturbative spin-orbit coupling correction to the total energy (needed e.g. for high-accuracy thermochemistry); NoSOCEnergy turns it off.

manual.section: 4.7.2 Spin-Orbit Coupling Correction to the Total Energy

purpose: Adds the diagonal Born-Oppenheimer correction, a first-order perturbation theory term needed in high-accuracy thermochemistry; implemented at SCF level, NoDBOC is the default-off switch.
requires: SCF level (HF/DFT) wavefunctions
typical_use: W4/HEAT-style thermochemistry protocols

purpose: Spin-orbit mean-field operator with fully numeric Coulomb terms (the pre-5.0 default combination of SOCType 3 with these flags).
requires: a CASSCF/MRCI or comparable multi-reference method that consumes the SOC operator; an auxiliary basis for the RI variants
defaults: SOCType 3, SOCFlags 1,4,3,0 (or 1,3,3,0 with RI and AuxJ available) and SOCMaxCenter 4 by default
typical_use: g-tensors, zero-field splitting, phosphorescence rate constants (EPR, ESD PHOSP inputs)

purpose: Mean-field SOC operator with a semi-numeric Coulomb term (one-center approximation); the widely used standard for g-tensor and ZFS work.
requires: a CASSCF/MRCI or comparable multi-reference method that consumes the SOC operator; an auxiliary basis for the RI variants
defaults: SOCType 3, SOCFlags 1,4,3,0 (or 1,3,3,0 with RI and AuxJ available) and SOCMaxCenter 4 by default
typical_use: g-tensors, zero-field splitting, phosphorescence rate constants (EPR, ESD PHOSP inputs)

purpose: Mean-field SOC operator variant with four-center Coulomb terms.
requires: a CASSCF/MRCI or comparable multi-reference method that consumes the SOC operator; an auxiliary basis for the RI variants
defaults: SOCType 3, SOCFlags 1,4,3,0 (or 1,3,3,0 with RI and AuxJ available) and SOCMaxCenter 4 by default
typical_use: g-tensors, zero-field splitting, phosphorescence rate constants (EPR, ESD PHOSP inputs)

purpose: RI approximation to the SOMF Coulomb term; requires an auxiliary basis even when the SCF itself uses no RI. Computationally more efficient than the semi-numeric variant with minimal error.
requires: a CASSCF/MRCI or comparable multi-reference method that consumes the SOC operator; an auxiliary basis for the RI variants
defaults: SOCType 3, SOCFlags 1,4,3,0 (or 1,3,3,0 with RI and AuxJ available) and SOCMaxCenter 4 by default
typical_use: g-tensors, zero-field splitting, phosphorescence rate constants (EPR, ESD PHOSP inputs)

purpose: RI approximation with the one-center Coulomb term; the keyword the manual uses in phosphorescence examples (ESD PHOSP).
requires: a CASSCF/MRCI or comparable multi-reference method that consumes the SOC operator; an auxiliary basis for the RI variants
defaults: SOCType 3, SOCFlags 1,4,3,0 (or 1,3,3,0 with RI and AuxJ available) and SOCMaxCenter 4 by default
typical_use: g-tensors, zero-field splitting, phosphorescence rate constants (EPR, ESD PHOSP inputs)

purpose: RI approximation with four-center Coulomb terms.
requires: a CASSCF/MRCI or comparable multi-reference method that consumes the SOC operator; an auxiliary basis for the RI variants
defaults: SOCType 3, SOCFlags 1,4,3,0 (or 1,3,3,0 with RI and AuxJ available) and SOCMaxCenter 4 by default
typical_use: g-tensors, zero-field splitting, phosphorescence rate constants (EPR, ESD PHOSP inputs)

purpose: DFT effective-potential SOC operator; suffers from not treating the spin-other-orbit exchange part, giving significant errors.
requires: a CASSCF/MRCI or comparable multi-reference method that consumes the SOC operator; an auxiliary basis for the RI variants
defaults: SOCType 3, SOCFlags 1,4,3,0 (or 1,3,3,0 with RI and AuxJ available) and SOCMaxCenter 4 by default
typical_use: g-tensors, zero-field splitting, phosphorescence rate constants (EPR, ESD PHOSP inputs)

purpose: DFT effective-potential SOC operator with the sign of the DFT exchange contribution reversed, which compensates the missing spin-other-orbit part within the DFT framework.
requires: a CASSCF/MRCI or comparable multi-reference method that consumes the SOC operator; an auxiliary basis for the RI variants
defaults: SOCType 3, SOCFlags 1,4,3,0 (or 1,3,3,0 with RI and AuxJ available) and SOCMaxCenter 4 by default
typical_use: g-tensors, zero-field splitting, phosphorescence rate constants (EPR, ESD PHOSP inputs)

purpose: The AMFI-like mean-field SOC setup (SOCType 3, one-center Coulomb, SOCMaxCenter 1); the deprecated AMFI-A variant uses pre-calculated atomic densities.
requires: a CASSCF/MRCI or comparable multi-reference method that consumes the SOC operator; an auxiliary basis for the RI variants
defaults: SOCType 3, SOCFlags 1,4,3,0 (or 1,3,3,0 with RI and AuxJ available) and SOCMaxCenter 4 by default
typical_use: g-tensors, zero-field splitting, phosphorescence rate constants (EPR, ESD PHOSP inputs)

purpose: Selects the relativistic Hamiltonian: DKH, ZORA, IORA or X2C (equivalent to the simple-input keywords).

Flags for the model potential used by the relativistic Hamiltonians: nuclear attraction, Coulomb (ZORA/IORA), Xalpha (ZORA/IORA), VWN-5 correlation (ZORA/IORA) and point charges (X2C); 1 includes a term, 0 leaves it out.
Selects the fitted atomic density used for the Coulomb model potential and the PModel guess: rhoDKH, rhoZORA or rhoHF.
If true, uses the one-center approximation of the model potential.
defaults: false in the block; enabled by default for DKH/ZORA analytic gradients

purpose: Speed of light used in atomic units; VELIT and VELOCITY are synonyms.
Controls the picture-change treatment of properties: 0 non-relativistic operator (default), 1 relativistic operator without derivatives of R and X, 2 full relativistic Hamiltonian derivative.
If true, uses the Gaussian finite-nucleus model; available for DKH and X2C (not ZORA) and relevant for hyperfine properties.
Amount of relativistics-related output (0-4); alias for the Print[P_Rel] output setting.
Order of the DKH Hamiltonian (1 or 2).
Chooses the Foldy-Wouthuysen transformation kind for EPR properties with DKH: true (fpFW, kinetic momentum) or false (fpiFW, gauge-invariant momentum).
Value of the Xalpha exchange parameter used by the model potential; only effective when VXa is included in ModelPot.
If true, scales the ZORA orbital energies (scaled ZORA variant); single points only.
If true, uses the diagonal local approximation of the X2C unitary transformation (X2C only; mutually exclusive with OneCenter).
Highest atomic number treated as non-relativistic within the DLU approximation.
X2C intermediate storage level (0-5).
